questions.question: Why is $\mathfrak c$ called the cardinality of the continuum?
options: It measures the length of a single vector
It counts the number of natural numbers
It measures the size of the real line
questions.explanation: The real line is the geometric continuum, and $\mathfrak c$ denotes the number of its points, i.e. $|\mathbb R|$.
questions.source_support: Interpretation: the continuum is the size of the real line.
option_explanations: Vector length is a real number attached to one vector, not a cardinality of a set.
Natural numbers are counted by $\aleph_0$, not $\mathfrak c$.

questions.question: How does $\mathfrak c$ compare with countable infinity?
options: It is smaller than every infinite cardinal

questions.explanation: Cantor's diagonal argument proves that $\mathbb R$ is uncountable, so $\mathfrak c=|\mathbb R|>\aleph_0$.

questions.skill_detail: Compare continuum size with aleph null.
